<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/maven-v4_0_0.xsd">
 <modelVersion>
  4.0.0
 </modelVersion>
 <parent>
  <groupId>
   org.sonatype.oss
  </groupId>
  <artifactId>
   oss-parent
  </artifactId>

   7

 <groupId>
  com.google.auto

  pom

  Auto (Parent)

  A collection of code generators for Java.

 <url>
  https://github.com/google/auto

 <properties>
  <project.build.sourceEncoding>
   UTF-8
  </project.build.sourceEncoding>

   1.6
  </java.version>
 </properties>
 <scm>
  <url>
   http://github.com/google/auto
  </url>

   scm:git:git://github.com/google/auto.git

   scm:git:ssh://git@github.com/google/auto.git

   HEAD
  </tag>

  <system>
   GitHub Issues
  </system>
  <url>
   http://github.com/google/auto/issues

   <name>
    Apache 2.0
   </name>
   <url>
    http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0.txt
   </url>
  </license>
 </licenses>
 <organization>
  <name>
   Google, Inc.
  </name>
  <url>
   http://www.google.com
  </url>
 </organization>
 <build>
  <plugins>
   <plugin>
    <groupId>
     org.apache.maven.plugins
    </groupId>
    <artifactId>
     maven-compiler-plugin
    </artifactId>
    <version>
     3.1
    </version>
    <configuration>
     <source>
      ${java.version}
     </source>
     <target>
      ${java.version}
     </target>
     <compilerArgument>
      -Xlint:all

     <showWarnings>
      true
     </showWarnings>
     <showDeprecation>
      true
     </showDeprecation>
    </configuration>
   </plugin>
   <plugin>
    <groupId>
     org.apache.maven.plugins
    </groupId>
    <artifactId>
     maven-checkstyle-plugin
    </artifactId>
    <version>
     2.11
    </version>
    <configuration>
     <consoleOutput>
      true
     </consoleOutput>
     <configLocation>
      checkstyle.xml
     </configLocation>

      false

   </plugin>
  </plugins>
  <pluginManagement>
   <plugins>
    <plugin>
     <artifactId>
      maven-invoker-plugin

      1.8

  <groupId>com.google.auto.factory</groupId>
  <artifactId>auto-factory</artifactId>
  <version>1.0-SNAPSHOT</version>
  <name>AutoFactory</name>
  <description>
    JSR-330-compatible factories.
  </description>

  <scm>
    <url>http://github.com/google/auto</url>
    <connection>scm:git:git://github.com/google/auto.git</connection>
    <developerConnection>scm:git:ssh://git@github.com/google/auto.git</developerConnection>
    <tag>HEAD</tag>
  </scm>

  <dependencies>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.auto</groupId>
      <artifactId>auto-common</artifactId>
      <version>0.5</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.auto.service</groupId>
      <artifactId>auto-service</artifactId>
      <version>1.0-rc2</version>
      <scope>provided</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.guava</groupId>
      <artifactId>guava</artifactId>
      <version>18.0</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.squareup</groupId>
      <artifactId>javawriter</artifactId>
      <version>2.5.1</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>javax.inject</groupId>

      <version>1</version>

      <artifactId>compile-testing</artifactId>
      <version>0.8</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>

      <groupId>junit</groupId>
      <artifactId>junit</artifactId>
      <version>4.12</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.truth</groupId>
      <artifactId>truth</artifactId>
      <version>0.25</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
  </dependencies>

  <build>
    <plugins>
      <plugin>
        <artifactId>maven-jar-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>2.5</version>
      </plugin>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
        <artifactId>maven-invoker-plugin</artifactId>
        <configuration>
          <addTestClassPath>true</addTestClassPath>
          <cloneProjectsTo>${project.build.directory}/it</cloneProjectsTo>
          <filterProperties>
            <auto.version>${project.version}</auto.version>
          </filterProperties>
          <pomIncludes>
            <pomInclude>*/pom.xml</pomInclude>
          </pomIncludes>
          <streamLogs>true</streamLogs>
        </configuration>
        <executions>
          <execution>
            <id>integration-test</id>
            <goals>
              <goal>install</goal>
              <goal>run</goal>
            </goals>
          </execution>
        </executions>
      </plugin>
    </plugins>
  </build>
</project>

<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
  xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/maven-v4_0_0.xsd">
  <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

  <parent>
    <groupId>com.google.auto</groupId>
    <artifactId>auto-parent</artifactId>
    <version>3</version>
  </parent>

  <groupId>com.google.auto.value</groupId>
  <artifactId>auto-value</artifactId>
  <version>1.2-SNAPSHOT</version>
  <name>AutoValue</name>
  <description>
    Immutable value-type code generation for Java 1.6+.
  </description>

  <properties>
    <guava.version>18.0</guava.version>
  </properties>
  <scm>
    <url>http://github.com/google/auto</url>
    <connection>scm:git:git://github.com/google/auto.git</connection>
    <developerConnection>scm:git:ssh://git@github.com/google/auto.git</developerConnection>
    <tag>HEAD</tag>
  </scm>

  <dependencies>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.auto</groupId>
      <artifactId>auto-common</artifactId>
      <version>1.0-SNAPSHOT</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.auto.service</groupId>
      <artifactId>auto-service</artifactId>
      <version>1.0-rc2</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.guava</groupId>
      <artifactId>guava</artifactId>
      <version>${guava.version}</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.ow2.asm</groupId>
      <artifactId>asm</artifactId>
      <version>4.1</version>
    </dependency>
    <!-- test dependencies -->
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.apache.velocity</groupId>
      <artifactId>velocity</artifactId>
      <version>1.7</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.guava</groupId>
      <artifactId>guava-testlib</artifactId>
      <version>${guava.version}</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.testing.compile</groupId>
      <artifactId>compile-testing</artifactId>
      <version>0.6</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>junit</groupId>
      <artifactId>junit</artifactId>
      <version>4.11</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.truth</groupId>
      <artifactId>truth</artifactId>
      <version>0.25</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
  </dependencies>

  <build>
    <resources>
      <resource>
        <directory>src/main/java</directory>
      </resource>
    </resources>
    <plugins>
      <plugin>
        <artifactId>maven-jar-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>2.5</version>
      </plugin>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
        <artifactId>maven-invoker-plugin</artifactId>
        <configuration>
          <addTestClassPath>true</addTestClassPath>
          <cloneProjectsTo>${project.build.directory}/it</cloneProjectsTo>
          <filterProperties>
            <auto.version>${project.version}</auto.version>
          </filterProperties>
          <pomIncludes>
            <pomInclude>*/pom.xml</pomInclude>
          </pomIncludes>
          <streamLogs>true</streamLogs>
        </configuration>
        <executions>
          <execution>
            <id>integration-test</id>
            <goals>
              <goal>install</goal>
              <goal>run</goal>
            </goals>
          </execution>
        </executions>
      </plugin>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.immutables.tools</groupId>
        <artifactId>maven-shade-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>3</version>
        <executions>
          <execution>
            <phase>package</phase>
            <goals>
              <goal>shade</goal>
            </goals>
            <configuration>
              <minimizeJar>true</minimizeJar>
              <relocations>
                <relocation>
                  <pattern>org.objectweb</pattern>
                  <shadedPattern>autovalue.shaded.org.objectweb$</shadedPattern>
                </relocation>
                <relocation>
                  <pattern>com.google</pattern>
                  <shadedPattern>autovalue.shaded.com.google$</shadedPattern>
                  <excludes>
                    <exclude>com.google.auto.value.**</exclude>
                  </excludes>
                </relocation>
              </relocations>
            </configuration>
          </execution>
        </executions>
      </plugin>
    </plugins>
  </build>
</project>

2. But that file doesn't exist in Java 11

I see the problem now. In compile-testing 0.7, the tools.jar dependency is directly in the main dependencies section (not conditional), and it relies on the `${toolsjar}` property being set by one of the profiles. The profile activation using `<exists>` should work to not activate when the file doesn't exist in Java 9+, but the dependency is still required.

The solution is to update compile-testing to a version that doesn't require tools.jar for Java 9+ (or exclude it). But looking at the newer versions, they all still have this conditional dependency.

Looking at compile-testing 0.21.0, it moved the tools.jar dependency into the profiles themselves (not in main dependencies), so it only applies if the profile is activated. This is the key difference!

The fix is to either:
1. Update compile-testing to a version >= 0.10 where the dependency was moved into profiles
2. Exclude the tools dependency from compile-testing

Version 0.15 has the tools.jar dependency moved to profiles. This is good, but it still requires Java 8 (has truth-java8-extension). Let me check what versions were still compatible with Java 6 (the project targets 1.6).

Actually, looking at the larger picture - the issue is that this codebase was designed for Java 6-8 and now it's being built on Java 11. The `tools.jar` was a standard part of the JDK up to Java 8, but in Java 9+ the APIs it contained were either moved to the core JDK or removed.

For annotation processors that need the compiler APIs in Java 9+, they should use the standard `javax.annotation.processing` and `javax.lang.model` packages that are part of the core JDK.

The simplest fix that maintains compatibility is to:

1. Exclude `com.sun:tools` from the `compile-testing` dependency since it's not needed in Java 9+ (the APIs are in the JDK now)
2. Remove the parent pom profiles for tools.jar since they're not needed in Java 9+

# Build Failure Analysis for google/auto

## Repository Location
/home/travis/build/failed/google/auto

## Error Summary
The build fails because the project depends on `com.sun:tools` (tools.jar) which does not exist in Java 9+. The environment is using Java 11.

## Detailed Error Messages
1. `Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27 at specified path /usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar`

This error occurs for the following modules:
- auto-common
- auto-factory
- auto-service
- auto-value

## Root Cause Analysis

### Problem 1: compile-testing dependency on tools.jar
The `compile-testing` library versions 0.6, 0.7, and 0.8 have a direct dependency on `com.sun:tools` in their main dependencies section. This dependency references `${toolsjar}` which is expected to point to `tools.jar`.

In Java 9+, the `tools.jar` file no longer exists. The compiler APIs that were previously in `tools.jar` have been moved into the core JDK.

### Problem 2: Parent pom.xml profiles for tools.jar
The parent pom.xml (/home/travis/build/failed/google/auto/pom.xml) contains profiles that set the `${toolsjar}` property:
- default-profile: activated if `${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar` exists
- mac-profile: activated if `${java.home}/../Classes/classes.jar` exists

In Java 11, neither of these files exists, so neither profile activates. However, the compile-testing dependency still tries to resolve the tools.jar.

### Problem 3: auto-value depends on auto-common:1.0-SNAPSHOT
The auto-value module depends on `com.google.auto:auto-common:jar:1.0-SNAPSHOT` which cannot be resolved from external repositories (it's a local snapshot). When building with the multi-module build-pom.xml, this should be resolved locally, but the build fails before auto-common can be installed.

## Fix Strategy

### Fix 1: Exclude tools dependency from compile-testing
Add exclusions for `com.sun:tools` from all `compile-testing` dependencies in the module pom files. This is safe because in Java 9+, the javax.annotation.processing and javax.lang.model APIs are part of the core JDK.

Files to modify:
- common/pom.xml
- factory/pom.xml
- service/pom.xml
- value/pom.xml

### Fix 2: Add Java 9+ profile to parent pom.xml
Add a profile for Java 9+ that defines an empty toolsjar property to prevent any residual issues. Actually, since we're excluding the dependency, this is not strictly necessary.

## Proposed Changes

### common/pom.xml
Add exclusion for com.sun:tools from compile-testing dependency:
```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>com.google.testing.compile</groupId>
  <artifactId>compile-testing</artifactId>
  <version>0.7</version>
  <scope>test</scope>
  <exclusions>
    <exclusion>
      <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
      <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
    </exclusion>
  </exclusions>
</dependency>
```

### factory/pom.xml
Same exclusion for compile-testing version 0.8

### service/pom.xml
Same exclusion for compile-testing version 0.6

### value/pom.xml
Same exclusion for compile-testing version 0.6

## Build Order
When using build-pom.xml:
1. Auto (Parent) - pom only
2. auto-common - must succeed first
3. auto-factory
4. auto-service
5. auto-value
6. build-only

# Build Failure Analysis for google/auto

## Repository Location
/home/travis/build/failed/google/auto

## Error Summary
The build fails because the project depends on `com.sun:tools` (tools.jar) which does not exist in Java 9+. The environment is using Java 11.

## Detailed Error Messages
1. `Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27 at specified path /usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar`

This error occurs for the following modules:
- auto-common
- auto-factory
- auto-service
- auto-value

## Root Cause Analysis

### Problem 1: compile-testing dependency on tools.jar
The `compile-testing` library versions 0.6, 0.7, and 0.8 have a direct dependency on `com.sun:tools` in their main dependencies section. This dependency references `${toolsjar}` which is expected to point to `tools.jar`.

In Java 9+, the `tools.jar` file no longer exists. The compiler APIs that were previously in `tools.jar` have been moved into the core JDK.

### Problem 2: Parent pom.xml profiles for tools.jar
The parent pom.xml (/home/travis/build/failed/google/auto/pom.xml) contains profiles that set the `${toolsjar}` property:
- default-profile: activated if `${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar` exists
- mac-profile: activated if `${java.home}/../Classes/classes.jar` exists

In Java 11, neither of these files exists, so neither profile activates. However, the compile-testing dependency still tries to resolve the tools.jar.

### Problem 3: auto-value depends on auto-common:1.0-SNAPSHOT
The auto-value module depends on `com.google.auto:auto-common:jar:1.0-SNAPSHOT` which cannot be resolved from external repositories (it's a local snapshot). When building with the multi-module build-pom.xml, this should be resolved locally, but the build fails before auto-common can be installed.

## Fix Strategy

### Fix 1: Exclude tools dependency from compile-testing
Add exclusions for `com.sun:tools` from all `compile-testing` dependencies in the module pom files. This is safe because in Java 9+, the javax.annotation.processing and javax.lang.model APIs are part of the core JDK.

Files to modify:
- common/pom.xml
- factory/pom.xml
- service/pom.xml
- value/pom.xml

### Fix 2: Add Java 9+ profile to parent pom.xml
Add a profile for Java 9+ that defines an empty toolsjar property to prevent any residual issues. Actually, since we're excluding the dependency, this is not strictly necessary.

## Proposed Changes

### common/pom.xml
Add exclusion for com.sun:tools from compile-testing dependency:
```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>com.google.testing.compile</groupId>
  <artifactId>compile-testing</artifactId>
  <version>0.7</version>
  <scope>test</scope>
  <exclusions>
    <exclusion>
      <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
      <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
    </exclusion>
  </exclusions>
</dependency>
```

### factory/pom.xml
Same exclusion for compile-testing version 0.8

### service/pom.xml
Same exclusion for compile-testing version 0.6

### value/pom.xml
Same exclusion for compile-testing version 0.6

## Build Order
When using build-pom.xml:
1. Auto (Parent) - pom only
2. auto-common - must succeed first
3. auto-factory
4. auto-service
5. auto-value
6. build-only

## Summary

I have successfully fixed the build errors in the google/auto Java codebase. Here's what was done:

### Step 1: Analysis
Identified two main issues causing the build to fail on Java 11:

1. **tools.jar dependency issue**: The `compile-testing` library versions 0.6, 0.7, and 0.8 have a direct dependency on `com.sun:tools` which points to `tools.jar` - a file that doesn't exist in Java 9+.

2. **javax.annotation.Generated missing**: The `javax.annotation.Generated` annotation was removed from the JDK in Java 9+ and needs to be provided by an external dependency.

### Step 2: Created diff files
Created 6 patch files in `/home/travis/build/failed/google/auto/`:
- `patch_1.diff` - Excludes tools dependency from compile-testing in common/pom.xml
- `patch_2.diff` - Excludes tools dependency from compile-testing in factory/pom.xml
- `patch_3.diff` - Excludes tools dependency from compile-testing in service/pom.xml
- `patch_4.diff` - Excludes tools dependency from compile-testing in value/pom.xml
- `patch_5.diff` - Adds javax.annotation-api dependency to factory/pom.xml
- `patch_6.diff` - Adds javax.annotation-api dependency to value/pom.xml

### Step 3: Applied changes
Applied all changes directly to the pom.xml files. The build now completes successfully with all 6 modules building:
- Auto (Parent)
- Auto Common Libraries
- AutoFactory
- AutoService
- AutoValue
- build-only
